subject: Cardinal Labs - onramp economics & platform fit
messages:
From: Ian Mercer <ian.mercer@cardinallabs.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cardinallabs.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cardinal Labs - follow-up: platform fit + pricing constraints

Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering and procurement teams finished an initial pass on Redwood's architecture and we like what we see — runtime performance looks solid for our low-latency inference needs. That said, Cardinal is in the final stages of a cost consolidation review and we have a competing vendor offering a substantially lower headline price for embeddings and completion tokens if we commit to their reserved bundle.

Before we can proceed to an internal recommendation, procurement asked us to check two things with Redwood:
1) Can you match or meaningfully bridge the headline unit economics (they're offering a 28% discount off list with a 24-month reserved commit)?
2) What packaging / migration assistance do you have for a low-risk switch (onboarding, pilot credits, execution support)?

I'm attaching a short RFP summary that procurement compiled. We value Redwood's runtime and the console features, but cost is the gating factor for Cardinal's Q1 vendor selection. If you have a quick-option scorecall this week to walk pricing levers, please propose a couple of times.

Best,
Ian Mercer
Head of Platform Partnerships
Cardinal Labs

Attachment: Cardinal_RFP_summary.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Mercer <ian.mercer@cardinallabs.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cardinal Labs - follow-up: platform fit + pricing constraints

Ian —

Appreciate the context and the RFP summary. Short answer: yes, we have levers to close the economics gap in many scenarios, and we can pair that with a low-risk onramp. High-level options we typically use to match headline economics:

- Committed reserved capacity (12–30% off list depending on term and GPU tier).
- Onboarding/pilot credits (3 months of token credits to remove migration risk).
- Bundled professional services for the migration window (we allocate an SE + runbook).
- Operational credits for egress or extended retention if that materially drives your run-rate.

To make a concrete counteroffer I need two items from your side: the target committed monthly token volume you’d consider, and whether a 24‑month term is a hard requirement or if a 12‑month with an up-front partial prepay would be acceptable.

I can do a 30-minute scorecall tomorrow at 10:00am PT or Thursday at 11:30am PT — happy to include our pricing ops lead (Lauren) to align on the model. I'm attaching a quicksheet that maps the levers to expected unit impacts so you can run the numbers with procurement.

If it helps, we have a standard 'migration-safe' term sheet that pairs a short pilot credit + a graded discount ramp for the first 6 months; I can draft a tailored version after the call.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142
Attachment: redwood-quicksheet-cardinal.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Cardinal Labs - follow-up: platform fit + pricing constraints

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Cardinal's RFP and Ian's ask. Quick internal read and recommended concessions below.

Quoted message (original):
> From: Ian Mercer <ian.mercer@cardinallabs.ai>
> Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
> Subject: Cardinal Labs - follow-up: platform fit + pricing constraints
>
> Jordan,
> ... (see attached)

Summary of our posture and suggested package: 
- Objective: win a 24-month renewal potential while keeping short-term risk low for Cardinal.
- Proposal (option A - competitive match):
  * 24-month commit, 28% blended discount target (to mirror their competing offer)
  * We give a 3-month pilot credit equal to ~15% of expected first-year consumption (offsets migration risk)
  * Dedicated onboarding SE and two-week tech migration sprint included at no additional charge
  * SLA addendum: 99.9% uptime + 2x credit on significant latency regressions during first 90 days
- Proposal (option B - staged ramp):
  * 12-month commit with 18% discount + upfront 40% prepay applied to first 6 months; 3-month pilot credits still included
  * Allows Cardinal to validate while giving Redwood earlier cash visibility

Questions for Marissa: acceptable to offer 28% blended in A if we secure a two-year commitment and commit to a migration credit? Any finance constraints on backloaded credits vs. upfront prepay?

If approved, I'll package option A as a 'last look' counter and include the SE/migration runbook.

—Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Mercer <ian.mercer@cardinallabs.ai>, procurement@cardinallabs.ai
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cardinal Labs - onramp economics & platform fit

Ian —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals. Attached is a tailored term sheet (Cardinal_term_sheet_v2.pdf) and a short summary below — this is our formal counter that aims to bridge to the 28% headline while preserving reasonable commitment structure.

Offer summary (final):
- Commit: 24-month term with a blended 26% discount on list pricing across completion and embedding units (we narrowed to 26% given infrastructure tiering).
- Pilot: 3-month onboarding credit equal to 12% of first-year expected consumption, redeemable during the first 90 days.
- Migration support: Dedicated SE + two-week migration sprint; two production run days included for benchmarking and KV cache tuning.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime with a 2x credit for any qualifying latency regressions in the first 90 days.
- Commercial mechanics: Net 30; option to prepay 40% for an additional 4% discount applied to year 1 only.

If Cardinal accepts this structure I will circulate an executable term sheet and schedule a technical kickoff with our SE to build the migration runbook. Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement confirmation of expected committed monthly token profile (baseline numbers to calculate pilot credit).
2) Sign-off on the term sheet — I can push an e-sign link once procurement confirms.
3) Kickoff SE onboarding (target within 7 business days of signed term sheet).
